newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Nuclear orders checks on plant.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Nuclear orders checks on plant.

text.p: Checks were ordered on Tuesday at Scottish Nuclear's Hunterston plant after "slight contamination" was found in tanks used to supply carbon dioxide to reactors, Scottish Nuclear said in a statement.

"Detailed investigations have shown that this may be associated with maintenance work carried out on a section of the reactor gas pipework resulting in a small amount of radioactive reactor gas passing back through a valve to the operational service tanks," the statement said.
Scottish Nuclear, part of British Energy Plc, said there was no risk to the public.

"It has to be stressed that although no transfer of radioactivity has been confirmed, in the event of this occurring, the increase in the level of radiation would not cause a hazard to public health," the statement said.
Further and more detailed checks were in hand, it added.
The Scottish Office said the risk to public health from the scare at Hunterston on the Ayrshire coast was negligible.

"I have looked carefully at all available information about the incident," Chief Medical Officer for Scotland Sir David Carter said in a statement. "At present the information and calculations provided indicate that the risk to public health - both adults and children - is negligible."
He said the companies concerned had arranged to sample potentially affected products to provide final reassurance that there had been no significant contamination.
First results will become available on Wednesday. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7715
